app.title: K 值预测平台 (K-value prediction platform)
app.summary: A person enters a compound structure as SMILES and the parts of a four-solvent mixture, and gets a predicted partition coefficient K, both raw and calibrated. For many compounds they upload a CSV or XLSX built from a downloadable template, get a prediction for every row with a count of rows that failed, and download the results. For one compound they can type or upload a few measured ratio–K points to correct the model, see the error before and after the correction, predict K at chosen ratios, and get a ranked list of solvent ratios close to a target K that leaves out ratios already tried or failed. The result is exported as a workbook. A separate tab shows how well the trained models perform.

task.text: Predict how a compound will partition across a four-solvent mixture, correct the prediction with a few measurements, and choose solvent ratios that give a target partition coefficient.

data.text: Tables of compounds given as SMILES strings, each paired with a four-part solvent ratio and, where it was measured, a partition coefficient K. Model outputs and evaluation tables are loaded from training artifacts.
data.item: a compound at one solvent ratio, with its measured or predicted K

stage.text: choosing a solvent system for a separation before running it, using a trained property model

mechanism.text: Tabs split the work. One gives an overview of the training data. Forms predict K for one compound or for an uploaded batch. A calibration tab combines an editable table of measured points with target and exclusion fields, then shows error metrics before and after correction plus tables of predictions and recommendations, all downloadable. An analysis tab compares the candidate models with bar, scatter, residual and partial-dependence charts.

field.text: machine-learning prediction of partition coefficients for choosing chromatography solvent systems in chemistry

workflow.name: predict a property under chosen conditions, correct it with a few measurements, and pick conditions that hit a target

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: The data overview tab shows counts of samples, compounds and ratios, the current model, a histogram of K, a bar chart of ratio coverage, and a preview of the training table.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Enter a SMILES and the hexane, ethyl acetate, methanol and water parts. Predicting shows calibrated and raw K and log10(K), the prediction mode, and the full result as JSON.
Download a CSV template, then upload a CSV or XLSX of SMILES with ratios. Every row is predicted, the results appear in a table, and failed rows are counted.

steps.step: correct the computation with a few known measurements
steps.here: Type 1–5 measured ratio–K points for one compound into an editable table, or upload them, and list the ratios to query. Running the calibration shows base and calibrated RMSE and MAE, the fitted calibrator, the fit at each point, and the calibrated predictions at the queried ratios.

steps.step: rank candidate conditions against a target
steps.here: Set a target K, how many ratios to return, and the ratios to exclude or already tried and failed. The calibration-first workflow returns a ranked list of recommended ratios with summary metrics.
Download batch or calibrated predictions as CSV or XLSX, or a workbook with summary, calibration points, query and recommendation sheets.

The model analysis tab compares candidate models and feature sets by error on new compounds. It shows true-versus-predicted and residual plots for the new-compound and known-compound protocols, feature importance, and partial dependence.

distinctive: The condition is a four-solvent mixture entered as parts (a:b:c:d) and normalized to fractions, so recommendations and calibration distances are worked out in ratio space.

The calibration method depends on how many measured points there are: an affine correction for 1–2 points, inverse-distance local residual correction for 3–5, and the measured value itself when a query matches a measured ratio. Error is reported before and after.
Recommendations leave out ratios that are excluded, already tested, or tried and failed, so the person is not offered a condition they have already run.

A prediction uses an exact match in measured or literature data first, then interpolation between ratios measured for the same compound, then the model, and the path taken is reported as the prediction mode.
Models are judged separately on new compounds (grouped by structure) and on known compounds, because predicting for an unseen compound is the hard case.
